dedupe_keys.name: a building height dataset across china in 2017 estimated by the spatially informed approach

description: A building height dataset across China in 2017 estimated by the spatially-informed approach is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Chen Yang et al. As a fundamental aspect of the urban form, building height is a key attribute for reflecting human activities and human-environment interactions in the urban context. However, openly accessible building height maps covering the whole China remain sorely limited, particularly for spatially informed data. Coverage: national (CN); published in 2022. Formats: GeoTIFF, Image. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 1750212 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
